guard: every manager-initiated stop names its path on the reap line, and a requested stop names the authenticated principal that asked, so an operator reading manager.<space>.log alone can tell one peer's despawn from another's, from a self-stop, from a recursive reap, and from a manager shutdown
why: #1423: all four stop paths used to render one sentence - `this manager stopped it (despawn or
shutdown)` - with no requester, and the shutdown teardown printed no line at all, so on a shared
host where several principals hold stop authority the log could not attribute a stop after the
fact. The requested-despawn cells drive the REAL doors (opStop through despawnCore and
despawnAuthorized) rather than a hand-built freeSlot string, because the point is that the
authenticated principal the door resolved reaches the line; a string-driven cell cannot prove

mutations.name: the rendered line drops the requesting principal
mutations.find: case "stopped-requested": return `this manager stopped it at ${cause.requester}'s request`;
mutations.expectRed: a requested despawn names the AUTHENTICATED principal that asked
mutations.cell: a requested despawn names the AUTHENTICATED principal that asked
mutations.note: The door still carries the cause and the line still prints, so only the requester-naming cell can catch it: exactly the attribution #1423 asks the log to carry.
